name: Paragon Hag
body:
Although some hags follow the path of modern witches, most hew to an older path. They gather lingering soul energy and use that free essence to fuel powerful magical workings, only some of which can be achieved through witchcraft alone.

The paragon hag learns magic more slowly than the witch, but also gains occult rituals that allow her coven to put other spellcasters to shame. She may also carry a focus for collected soul energy to aid in her misdeeds.

Scheming, clever, and brutal, the paragon hag is a terrible enemy. Her familial link reflects a bloodline passed from mother to daughter from the mists of time, and this power grows in prominence as she gains experience. Covens are an important foundation for the paragon hag’s power, providing seemingly unbridled power beyond that of the greatest wizards. Even in close combat, a paragon hag rips apart her adversaries with vicious talons and surprising strength.

Role: The paragon hag is strongest outside of battle, using her magic to avoid fights or cripple enemies before the battle even begins. Once battle is joined, however, she tears into foes with her claws and curses.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d8.

Requirements

To qualify to become a paragon hag, a character must be any form of hag (while Paragon Hags are usually hags or changelings, any race may begin its decent into becoming a hag).

Starting Wealth: 3d6 x 10 gp (average 105 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The paragon hag’s class skills are Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Craft (any) (Int), Disguise (Cha), Fly (Dex), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (any) (Int), Perception (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), Survival (Wis), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks Per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Class Features

The following are class features of the paragon hag.

Weapon And Armor Proficiencies

A paragon hag is proficient with all simple weapons. They are not proficient with any type of armor or shields. Armor interferes with a paragon hag’s gestures, which can cause her spells with somatic components to fail.

Spellcasting

A paragon hag casts arcane spells from the witch spell list. She can cast any spell she knows without preparing it ahead of time.

To learn or cast a spell, the paragon hag must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a paragon hag’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the paragon hag’s Charisma modifier.

Like other spellcasters, a paragon hag can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Her base daily spell allotment is given on Table: Paragon Hag. In addition, she receives bonus spells per day if she has a high Charisma score.

The paragon hag’s selection of spells is extremely limited. A paragon hag begins play knowing four 0-level spells and two 1st-level spells of the paragon hag’s choice. At each new paragon hag level, she gains one or more new spells, as indicated on Table: Paragon Hag Spells Known. (Unlike spells per day, the number of spells a paragon hag knows is not affected by her Charisma score. The numbers on Table: Paragon Hag Spells Known are fixed.)

Upon reaching 5th level, and at every third paragon hag level thereafter (8th, 11th, 14th, 17th, and 20th), a paragon hag can choose to learn a new spell in place of one she already knows. In effect, the paragon hag “loses” the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged, and it must be at least one level lower than the highest-level paragon hag spell the paragon hag can cast. A paragon hag may swap only a single spell at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that she gains new spells known for the level.

A paragon hag need not prepare her spells in advance. She can cast any spell she knows at any time, assuming she has not yet used up her allotment of spells per day for the spell’s level.

Cantrips: Paragon hags learn a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells, as noted on Table: Paragon Hag Spells Known under “Spells Known.” These spells are cast like any other spells, but do not consume a slot and may be used again.

Family

Each paragon hag traces her lineage back to a grandmother back in the mists of time. This family connection grants the paragon hag a number of powers as she levels.

At 1st level, 4th level, and every four levels thereafter, a paragon hag gains a special power from her family.

At 3rd level, and every three levels thereafter, a paragon hag learns an additional spell determined by her family. These spells are in addition to the spells listed on Table: Paragon Hag Spells Known and cannot be exchanged at higher levels.

Hag’s Claws

The paragon hag’s nails harden into terrible claws. These claws are treated as natural weapons, allowing her to make two claw attacks as a full attack action. The claws deal damage as indicated on Table: Paragon Hag, unless the paragon hag already has claws that deal more damage.

At 2nd level, these claws are considered magical for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

At 6th level, the paragon hag’s claws are treated as cold iron and silver for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

At 10th level, these claws threaten a critical hit on a roll of 19–20. The hag’s claws changes to critical threat range are inherent to the claws, stacking with the keen enchantment and similar effects.

At 14th level, her claws damage incorporeal creatures as though they had the ghost touch weapon enchantment.

At 18th level, the claws threaten a critical hit on a roll of 18–20.

Hag-Like

Paragon hags count as hags for the purpose of qualifying for feats, abilities, spell targeting and similar effects.

Occult Coven

A paragon hag can form a coven as long as there are at least two other members willing and able to join. The paragon hag’s coven does not necessarily grant the same powers as given by monstrous hags’ covens, but can if she is a monstrous hag or a monstrous hag is counted among its members. See Covens above for more detail on covens.

A paragon hag may grant a number of sentient creatures up to her Charisma modifier the ability to join her coven. This is in addition to any members who qualify through their own abilities. She may retract an invitation or dismiss a coven member invited with this ability at will, but cannot grant it to a new creature for 24 hours after that. If her Charisma modifier is lowered, she must retract an appropriate number of invitations or dismiss a number of invited coven members.

Whenever a member of a paragon hag’s coven fails a skill check that is part of an occult ritual, the paragon hag may spend a soul point to allow that character to reroll the check. They must take the second result, even if it is lower.

Soul Focus (Su)

At 1st level, paragon hags form a powerful bond with an object. The bonded object serves as a receptacle for magical energy in the form of soul points.

Objects being used as a soul focus must fall into one of the following categories: amulet, book, broom, cauldron, dagger, ring, shawl, or staff. Paragon hags begin play with the object at no cost; it is always of masterwork quality. Objects acquired at 1st level are not made of any special material.

Amulet, ring, and shawl soul focuses must be worn to have effect, taking up a neck, ring, or shoulder slot respectively. Books, brooms, daggers, and staves must be held in hand. Cauldrons must be set on a flat surface and filled with liquid, but have effect as long as they are within 30 feet of the paragon hag.

If a paragon hag attempts to cast a spell without her soul focus, she must make a concentration check or lose the spell. The DC for this check is 20 + the spell’s level.

If a soul focus is destroyed or lost, a paragon hag may create a new one with a masterwork object of the appropriate type. This ritual requires a week, but has no risk of failure.

The soul focus holds a number of soul points equal to the paragon hag’s Charisma modifier (minimum 1). The soul points are replenished in full whenever the paragon hag prepares spells and may be filled by other actions related to her lineage, but can never exceed this maximum. If the paragon hag is not under the effect of her soul focus, she cannot use her soul points for any purpose.

Once per day, she may cast a paragon hag spell without expending a spell slot by instead spending a number of soul points equal to the spell’s level. She can do this even if she has used all her spell slots of that level already. She can use this ability one additional time per day at 6th, 11th, and 16th level.

Occult Proficiency

At 5th level, a paragon hag gains a +2 competence bonus on all skill checks made as part of an occult ritual. This bonus increases to +4 at 10th level and +6 at 15th.

When starting an occult ritual, a paragon hag may choose to halve the casting time of the ritual. Skill checks are evenly distributed across this time.

Further, if the paragon hag succeeds on every skill check required by an occult ritual, that ritual’s caster level is increased by two. This bonus does not increase with level, but can stack with multiple paragon hags.

Ritual Spells (Su)

At 5th level and every two levels thereafter, the paragon hag learns an occult ritual version of a particular spell as determined by her family.

To complete these rituals, the paragon hag must be the primary caster of the ritual. These rituals also require at least two secondary casters and all secondary casters must be part of the paragon hag’s coven.

The first ritual spell each paragon hag gains is a 4th level ritual. The subsequent rituals are each one higher than the last, eventually exceeding traditional 9th level spells.

Some ritual spells have metamagic feats applied to them. The casters do not need to possess those metamagic feats, but the spells’ levels are affected as normal.

The ritual requires a number of successful checks equal to its level, with half of those (rounded up) being Knowledge (arcana) checks and the other half being determined by the family’s listed ritual skill. The DC of each check is 25 + the ritual’s level.

The backlash from the ritual is 1d4 Charisma damage. If this damage is prevented or healed through magic, she cannot participate in any occult ritual until she next prepares spells.

A failed ritual prevents all participants from being a caster in the same ritual for 30 days.

Ritual spells require the same focus and material components as the spells they emulate and are consumed as normal. Certain ritual spells may be rendered permanent through use of the permanency spell, but require the same costs and components described in that spell.

Hag’s Curse (Sp)

At 7th level, paragon hags can cast bestow curse as a spell-like ability by expending a soul point.

At 17th level, the curse acts as greater bestow curse instead.

Shared Souls (Su)

At 13th level, a paragon hag may use the soul points of any other paragon hag in her coven as long as the other member is willing and has access to her soul focus.

Any non-hag member can sacrifice an arcane spell once per day as a standard action, as though that spell was just cast. When they do, they grant any single paragon hag in the coven soul points equal to the sacrificed spell’s level. Points in excess of the hag’s maximum are lost.

Occult Fortune (Su)

At 19th level, when performing any skill checks or saving throws for an occult ritual, a paragon hag may always roll two dice and take the better result.
